summary: Verified 6.8, not on par: one confirmed sensitivity blocker. Splash art is unchanged since 8b93ac403. Base splash.png at 1:1 shows the face fully wrapped in horizontal bands inside the hood, with no eave, no slit and no eyes: a mummy read. The Highrim splash head is tilted to the sky and reads as a blank white egg. Owner ruling 2 already treats a face that reads blank at portrait size as a sensitivity issue. The Long Evening splash, the portraits and the icon do show a warm eye slit, so the fix is local to two cards. The posterized cut-out quality of the splashes is confirmed as a major. The recall clip was re-checked on a shot taken after the current GLB (GLB Nov 6 19:51, shot Nov 7 14:44): the lens frame cuts through the hood at face height in every frame. I downgraded it to minor because the only view where the cut is legible is the eye-level close camera. At the 52 degree game camera, the frame over the hood reads as holding the lens close (closing_kemdo_r2_game_x3.png). The gameplay model is solid: rounded hood, crown gate 3/3 pass (R3 13.9 cm, re-run now), clear lens ellipse, robe spring bones, distinct deluxe. The in-game hood does not read as pointed, horror or mannequin. Timing was not measured (load 11.8-39 at review time).

findings.title: Base and Highrim splash heads read as a featureless wrapped/blank oval (mummy / blank mannequin)
findings.what: Base splash: the whole face is horizontal linen wraps inside the hood, with no eave shadow, no slit and no eyes, so it reads as a mummy. Highrim splash: the head is tipped back and reads as a smooth white egg. The brief (kemdo.md:55) calls for a carved brow eave over a narrow ink slit. Long Evening splash, the portraits and the icon all show the warm slit with eyes, so the problem is limited to these two cards, which appear in the shop, collection, draft and loading screens.
findings.evidence: Viewed art/out/fighters/kemdo/splash.png and kemdo_highrim_splash.png at full size; crops _harness/_shots/closing_kemdo_splash_face_x3.png and closing_kemdo_highrim_splash_face_x3.png. Contrast closing_kemdo_le_splash_face_x3.png and closing_kemdo_r2_portraits.png, where the eyes read. Splash files last changed in 8b93ac403. Precedent: owner_rulings.md:24 (ruling 2) treats a face that reads blank at portrait size as a sensitivity issue.
findings.gauge: LoL splashes always give a hooded or wrapped champion a living focal point: eyes, a lit slit or a readable profile. They never show a blank head.
findings.fix: Re-pose the base and Highrim card cameras 3/4 front-low with the head tilt at 20 degrees or less, so the sandstone eave and the warm skin slit with two catch-lit eyes are in frame. Use the same face read as the Long Evening card and the portrait. Add a darker under-eave band so the wraps are not one value.
findings.files: art/blender/fighters/kemdo.py (SPLASH / skin card camera), art/out/fighters/kemdo/splash.png, kemdo_highrim_splash.png
findings.verifierNote: I could not refute it. At 1:1 neither card has any eye or slit pixels, and the Highrim head is a single pale value. This is the blank-mannequin class from the standing rule, consistent with ruling 2. Severity holds.

findings.title: Splash cards are posterized 3D cut-outs with stair-step edges, flat-lit against the plate
findings.what: All three cards composite a posterized render with blocky facets and aliased silhouettes onto a painted plate. The figure is lit flat, with no plate-sun key, no rim and no contact shadow beyond a faint smear. It sits small at the right, about 55% of frame height. The brief's beat (kemdo.md:128, :178) is missing: no stone under the boot, and no glint at the top of the frame on the base lens.
findings.gauge: LoL splashes are fully painted with integrated light and composition, and never show render artifacts or a cut-out figure.
findings.fix: Render at 2x with the plate's key light and a warm rim, and drop the posterize filter. Do a paint-over pass to unify the edges, add a contact shadow and the low stone, make the lens glint the focal point, and scale the figure to about 75% of frame height on a thirds line.
findings.verifierNote: The defects are plainly visible at 1600x900. Major is right: it is quality, not sensitivity.

findings.title: Recall drives the lens frame through the hood/face in every frame
findings.what: The interpenetration is real in all sampled frames, captured after the current GLB. It is legible only at the eye-level close camera. At the 52 degree game camera, the frame over the hood reads as holding the lens close to the face. Recall is not shown in the store or loading cards.
findings.evidence: _harness/_shots/closing_kemdo_clip_recall_x2.png (shot dated Nov 7 14:44, GLB dated Nov 6 19:51); game-camera read in closing_kemdo_r2_game_x3.png.
findings.gauge: LoL recalls show no visible interpenetration, but they are judged at the game camera.
findings.fix: Hold the lens 25-30 cm in front of the eave, tilted down, and shade it with the free hand. Run the clip probe with the hood as a collider.
findings.verifierNote: Downgraded from major: the clip is real, but it is not legible at the camera players use, and the clip has no card or store exposure.

findings.title: Held Focus reads as holding a plate at chest, not a lens aimed at the target
findings.what: In the ult and channel rows of closing_kemdo_clips.png, the lens lies near horizontal at chest height.
findings.gauge: An ultimate holds a distinct, legible key pose.
findings.fix: Raise the frame to head height and tip the lens about 60 degrees toward the target.

findings.title: No signature-hue zone: beige figure on a beige lane separates by value only
findings.what: Only the lens ring carries colour.
findings.gauge: LoL champions carry a signature hue patch.
findings.fix: Dye the waist wrap and frame bindings a desaturated kiln-terracotta outside the marigold band.
findings.verifierNote: Kept as minor. Value separation is adequate in the game frame.

findings.title: Long Evening splash reads cream and pink, not plum
findings.what: The wraps dominate the card, and the plum shows only on the sleeve and lower body.
findings.gauge: Deluxe splashes lead with the theme colour.
findings.fix: Frame the card on the lantern hem and sash, and grade the plate warmer.

findings.title: At eye-level close views the face wrap reads as a pale oval with a dark stripe
findings.what: Every row of the clip sheet shows a pale face oval with a thin dark band. It is not a sensitivity read at game scale, where the hood dominates (closing_kemdo_r2_game_x3.png).
findings.gauge: Hooded LoL champions show an eye read at close range.
findings.fix: Paint a warm skin strip with two catch-lit eyes into the slit, and deepen the eave shadow.
findings.verifierNote: Kept as minor. The model is seen close only in the clip viewer. The cards are the exposed surface and are covered by B1.
